aidb_assessment.novelty: High as an evaluation package: it combines long-duration GPU infrastructure tasks at three abstraction levels with private judging, instruction review, trajectory analysis, and an equal-compute horizon comparison. The individual optimization methods are less uniformly novel, but the agent-discovered codec is a substantive case study.
aidb_assessment.rationale: The paper offers consequential evidence that short evaluations can mis-rank agents and particularly understate system-level performance. Its controlled equal-compute comparison and detailed failure cases make it decision-relevant. Adoption as a canonical leaderboard should wait for repeated runs, harness-controlled comparisons, Controller validation, and independent reproduction. The codec result is promising but remains one selected case with mixed decoding efficiency and dataset-selection caveats.
aidb_assessment.usefulness: High for studying long-horizon coding agents, benchmark design, delayed optimization gains, evaluator robustness, and infrastructure discovery. The task suite and trajectories can support research beyond a single leaderboard, especially failure analysis and allocation of agent compute.

executive_summary: Infrathon evaluates language agents on real AI-infrastructure optimization rather than short, isolated coding tasks. Its 25 tasks span operator, module, and system levels, with private evaluation and 12–24-hour runs. The strongest evidence is that evaluation duration changes conclusions: rankings shift early, most runs improve in their second half, and equal-compute long runs strongly outperform best-of-four short runs on systems, though not operators. Claude Opus 5.5 leads overall and produces a KV-cache codec that improves compression and video-quality metrics over a human codec. However, the main leaderboard uses one selected run per task–model pair, different agent harnesses, and heterogeneous rank aggregation. Controller rejections, incorrect performance tests, and premature stopping reveal substantial validity risks. The benchmark is valuable and unusually instrumented, but broader replication and variance estimates are needed before treating its model ordering as stable.

assumptions: Private tests and Controller review adequately detect invalid optimizations and reward hacking.
Best-so-far private score is an appropriate measure even when agents receive repeated private-test feedback.

key_components: Infrathon-build supports expert construction of long-horizon tasks from open-source and research infrastructure projects.
Work, Controller, and Judge environments separate agent development, rule checking, and private evaluation.
Operator tasks receive shorter budgets than module and system tasks; tool execution and feedback waits count against the budget.
The Controller uses GPT-6.1 Sol in Codex to inspect instruction following and possible reward hacking before private scoring.
Final performance is the best valid private-test score within the budget; overall ordering uses equal-weighted within-task ranks.
The controlled horizon comparison allocates equal GPU-hours to one full run, two half-length runs, or four quarter-length runs.
The codec case study uses fixed generation settings and compares compression, reconstruction, perceptual, and full-video quality.
method.overview: Infrathon defines each task through a workspace, public tests, private tests, resources, and a time budget. An agent works iteratively in a Work environment. A trusted Controller limits and reviews submissions, including an LLM-based instruction-following check, before a separate Judge executes hidden tests. The principal study takes the best valid private score obtained within each run, then aggregates within-task model ranks with equal task weights. Additional analyses compare full-horizon runs against independent shorter runs under equal GPU-hour budgets, inspect score trajectories, and manually analyze behavioral failures. A case study compares an agent-designed KV-cache codec against a human codec on fixed video-generation inputs.

open_questions: How much variance appears across independent full-budget repetitions for every task–model pair?
Would the model ranking persist if every model used the same agent harness, prompts, tool interfaces, and stopping mechanism?
What are the Controller’s false-accept and false-reject rates against blinded expert review?
How much does repeated private-test feedback contribute to performance, and does it induce evaluator overfitting?
Do the horizon findings generalize beyond the six selected tasks and the two models in the equal-compute comparison?
Does the Claude codec retain its advantage on unseen video models, datasets, hardware, and end-to-end serving workloads?
What deployment trade-off emerges when cache lifetime, number of decodes, encode latency, decode latency, and memory savings are combined in one cost model?

problem.importance: Infrastructure optimization requires iterative implementation, profiling, and validation; a short evaluation can miss delayed improvements, regressions, and changes in relative model performance.
problem.scope: The study covers 25 optimization tasks: 11 operator, 5 module, and 9 system tasks, divided into 10 training and 15 inference tasks. It evaluates six models on H100-based environments, with separate public-development and private-judging paths.
problem.statement: The paper asks whether frontier language agents can repeatedly improve real-world AI infrastructure over extended executions while maintaining correctness and respecting task-specific hardware and implementation constraints.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The paper’s single selected main run for each task–model pair and its equal-weighted rank score.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: The reported overall ordering is stable under independent repetitions, but confidence intervals will overlap for some middle-ranked models and task groups.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Bootstrap confidence interval for each model’s mean rank score across at least three independently seeded full-budget repetitions per task–model pair, plus the probability of each pairwise ordering.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop when every pair has completed the preregistered repetition count and either each adjacent ordering exceeds a 95% posterior probability or the study concludes that the ordering is unresolved.

proposed_experiments.baseline: The original split in which Claude uses Claude Code and the other models use Codex CLI.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: A common harness will reduce the observed performance gap between Claude Opus 5.5 and GPT-6 Astra, showing that part of the leaderboard difference is attributable to agent scaffolding.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Change in within-task rank score and task wins under a crossed model-by-harness design with identical budgets, prompts, tool permissions, submission limits, and stop hooks.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after balanced repeated runs cover the preregistered task subset and the confidence interval for the harness interaction is narrow enough to distinguish a practically meaningful rank-score change from no meaningful effect.

proposed_experiments.baseline: GPT-6.1 Sol Controller decisions used by the benchmark.
proposed_experiments.hypothesis: Expert-audited rule checking will identify both missed violations and false rejections from the LLM Controller, and these errors will alter some best-so-far trajectories.
proposed_experiments.primary_metric: Blinded expert adjudication agreement, false-accept rate, false-reject rate, and resulting change in final task winners after replaying disputed submissions.
proposed_experiments.stop_condition: Stop after all rejected submissions and a stratified sample of accepted submissions reach double-review consensus, with disagreements resolved by a third reviewer.

reproducibility.assessment: The methodological description is unusually detailed, including software versions, hardware allocations, scoring formulas, and experimental budgets. However, exact replay remains uncertain because the evidence does not identify immutable code and environment versions, model API snapshots, or complete raw artifacts. The reliance on proprietary model endpoints and a model-based Controller further limits exact reproducibility. Independent reproduction of aggregate conclusions appears possible if the repository contains the stated assets, but this cannot be verified from the supplied material alone.

results.result: Late improvement is common: 135 of 150 runs improve during the second half; among runs with positive first-half scores, the median gain is 3.05%, and 33 runs gain more than 10%. The effect is uneven, so the result supports longer measurement more strongly than it supports uniformly large gains.

results.result: With equal GPU-hours, four short runs achieve 102.6% of one long run on operators, 96.9% on modules, and only 77.3% on systems. The full-horizon condition wins nine of 12 task–model comparisons and every system comparison, indicating that continuity matters most for end-to-end work.

results.result: On the codec case study, Claude’s design raises WorldScore compression from 6.75× to 20.89× while PSNR rises from 31.15 to 36.33, SSIM from 0.923 to 0.975, and LPIPS falls from 0.059 to 0.023. On MovieGen, compression rises from 6.88× to 18.83×, with all three frame-quality metrics also improving.
